title: Decorative button effects
description: Gradient fills and opacity changes on action controls can weaken the action hierarchy or readability.
guidance: Review the rendered default, hover, focus and pending states. Prefer the accepted accent and stable label contrast when decoration contributes no useful state information.
verification: Compare the real action at desktop and mobile widths in default, hover, keyboard focus and loading states; measure label contrast against its actual background.
counterexamples: A deliberate branded gradient or an opacity-based disabled state can be appropriate; the source pattern alone is not a defect.

title: Decorative hero blur
description: A blurred hero or authentication background may compete with content or add unnecessary rendering work.
guidance: Inspect the actual background, text contrast and performance. Remove atmospheric blur when it has no role in the accepted visual system.
verification: Compare the rendered hero and auth form with the effect enabled and disabled, including narrow viewports and reduced motion.
counterexamples: A purposeful image blur or a supported brand treatment can be appropriate; selector names do not prove visible decoration.

title: Persistent field labels
description: Placeholder-only fields lose their visible instruction as soon as a person enters text.
guidance: Give fields a persistent visible label where needed; retain the accessible name and use placeholders for examples. Review search or compact controls in context.
verification: Enter text, autofill and submit invalid data. Confirm the field remains identifiable, its error is understandable and its programmatic name is correct.
counterexamples: A search field with an unambiguous adjacent control or a space-constrained, well-named control may not need an additional visible label.

title: Disabled token-signature verification
description: Decoding a token without signature verification must not establish an authenticated identity or authorization.
guidance: Trace the decoded claims to their use. Verify signatures, issuer, audience and expiry through the trusted identity service before making authorization decisions.
verification: Use signed, tampered, expired, wrong-issuer and unsigned tokens against the relevant operation; confirm only the authorized identity is accepted.
counterexamples: Unverified decoding for display or diagnostics is acceptable only when no security decision trusts the result.
